shorts.title: The Day the Mona Lisa Vanished
shorts.covers: In 1911 a handyman walked out of the Louvre with the Mona Lisa under his smock, and the world's most famous painting was missing for two years.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

script.title: The Day the Mona Lisa Vanished
script.description: In 1911 a handyman walked out of the Louvre with the Mona Lisa hidden under his smock. For two years nobody knew where it was, and the empty space on the wall drew bigger crowds than the painting ever had.

shorts.title: The Man Who Sold the Eiffel Tower
shorts.covers: In 1925 a con man called Victor Lustig convinced scrap metal dealers that Paris was selling the Eiffel Tower, and took their money.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

script.title: The Man Who Sold the Eiffel Tower
script.description: In 1925 a con man read that the Eiffel Tower was expensive to repair. He posed as a government official, called in scrap metal dealers, and sold it to one of them.

shorts.title: The First Murder Solved by a Fingerprint
shorts.covers: In 1892 in Argentina, a bloody thumbprint on a door frame revealed who had killed two children, the first murder solved by fingerprints.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

script.title: The First Murder Solved by a Fingerprint
script.description: In 1892, in a small town in Argentina, two children were killed and their mother blamed a neighbour. A police inspector found a bloody thumbprint on a door frame, and it pointed somewhere else.

shorts.title: Escape From Alcatraz
shorts.covers: In 1962 three men slipped out of the most secure prison in America using spoons, fake heads made of plaster and a raft of raincoats.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

script.title: Escape From Alcatraz
script.description: In June 1962 three men vanished from the most secure prison in America, leaving dummy heads made of plaster in their beds. They were never seen again.

shorts.title: Charley Ross: The First Ransom Kidnapping
shorts.covers: In 1874 two men lured a four-year-old boy into a wagon in Philadelphia, and America learned what a ransom note was.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

script.title: Charley Ross: The First Ransom Kidnapping
script.description: In 1874 two men in a horse-drawn wagon offered sweets to two small boys outside their home in Philadelphia. Only one came back, and America learned what a ransom note was.

shorts.title: Lizzie Borden and the Axe
shorts.covers: In 1892 a couple were killed with a hatchet in Fall River, Massachusetts, and their daughter was tried and acquitted.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

script.title: Lizzie Borden and the Hatchet
script.description: In 1892 a wealthy couple were killed with a hatchet in their home in Fall River, Massachusetts. Their daughter Lizzie was charged with the murders, tried, and acquitted.

shorts.title: The Zodiac Cipher, Cracked After Fifty Years
shorts.covers: The Zodiac killer sent police coded letters in 1969, and in 2020 three amateur codebreakers finally solved one of them.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: How Al Capone Was Really Caught
shorts.covers: The most famous gangster in America was never convicted of violence, and in 1931 he went to prison for not paying his taxes.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Kim Philby: The Spy at the Top
shorts.covers: A senior British intelligence officer had been working for the Soviet Union for decades, and slipped away to Moscow in 1963.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Adolf Beck: The Wrong Man Twice
shorts.covers: In 1896 an innocent man was convicted of crimes committed by a lookalike, and his case led to Britain's Court of Criminal Appeal.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Antwerp Diamond Heist
shorts.covers: In 2003 thieves beat ten layers of security at the Antwerp Diamond Centre, and were caught because of a half-eaten sandwich dumped in a forest.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Charles Ponzi and His Famous Scheme
shorts.covers: In 1920 a man in Boston promised investors huge profits from postal coupons, and paid early investors with new investors' money.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Marie Lafarge and the Arsenic Test
shorts.covers: In 1840 a French widow was tried for poisoning her husband, and a new chemical test for arsenic was put on trial with her.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Wooden Keys of Pretoria Prison
shorts.covers: In 1979 three political prisoners in South Africa carved wooden keys for ten locked doors and walked out of a maximum security jail.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Kidnapping of Frank Sinatra Jr
shorts.covers: In 1963 the singer's nineteen-year-old son was taken from a hotel room at Lake Tahoe, and released after his father paid.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: 10 Rillington Place
shorts.covers: In 1950 Timothy Evans was hanged for murders in a London house, and three years later the real killer was found living there.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Somerton Man
shorts.covers: In 1948 a man was found dead on an Australian beach with a scrap of paper reading 'it is finished' sewn into his trousers.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The St Valentine's Day Massacre
shorts.covers: In 1929 gunmen dressed as police lined seven men up against a garage wall in Chicago, and the killing turned the public against the gangs.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Klaus Fuchs: The Atomic Spy
shorts.covers: A physicist on the atomic bomb project passed its secrets to Moscow, and confessed in 1950 to a British interrogator.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Oscar Slater: Eighteen Years for Nothing
shorts.covers: In 1909 a man was convicted of a Glasgow murder on weak evidence, and Arthur Conan Doyle campaigned for his release.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Hatton Garden: The Pensioners' Heist
shorts.covers: Over an Easter weekend in 2015, a gang of men in their sixties and seventies drilled through a vault wall in London's jewellery quarter.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Country That Did Not Exist
shorts.covers: In the 1820s Gregor MacGregor sold land, titles and passage to Poyais, a Central American country he had invented, and settlers sailed to find it.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Jigsaw Murders
shorts.covers: In 1935 body parts were found in a Scottish ravine, and scientists rebuilt the victims from them, using a photograph to prove who one of them was.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Ronnie Biggs Goes Over the Wall
shorts.covers: In 1965 one of the Great Train Robbers escaped from Wandsworth Prison over a rope ladder and spent decades on the run.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Getty Kidnapping
shorts.covers: In 1973 the grandson of the richest man in the world was kidnapped in Rome, and his grandfather refused to pay until an ear arrived in the post.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Let Him Have It: Derek Bentley
shorts.covers: In 1953 a nineteen-year-old was hanged for a shooting he did not commit, over four words whose meaning was argued for decades.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Isdal Woman
shorts.covers: In 1970 a burned body was found in a Norwegian valley, with false identities, coded notes and labels cut from every piece of clothing.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Kray Twins
shorts.covers: Twin brothers ran a criminal empire in 1960s London, mixing with celebrities, until a detective called Nipper Read brought them down.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Rosenbergs
shorts.covers: In 1953 an American couple were executed for passing atomic secrets to the Soviet Union, in a case that still divides opinion.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Stefan Kiszko: The Science That Freed Him
shorts.covers: In 1976 a shy tax clerk was convicted of a murder he could not have committed, and medical evidence proved it sixteen years later.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Gardner Museum Robbery
shorts.covers: In 1990 two men dressed as police officers talked their way into a Boston museum and left with thirteen works of art that have never been found.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Tichborne Claimant
shorts.covers: In the 1860s a butcher from Australia claimed to be the lost heir to a great English fortune, and the heir's mother accepted him.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Acid Bath Murderer
shorts.covers: In 1949 John Haigh believed that dissolving his victims in acid meant he could never be convicted, and a few gallstones proved him wrong.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Dillinger's Wooden Gun
shorts.covers: In 1934 the bank robber John Dillinger escaped from an Indiana jail using a gun he had carved from wood and blackened with shoe polish.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Chowchilla Bus Kidnapping
shorts.covers: In 1976 three men hijacked a school bus in California and buried twenty-six children in a truck underground. The children dug their way out.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Ruth Ellis: The Last Woman Hanged
shorts.covers: In 1955 a nightclub manager shot her lover outside a London pub, and became the last woman executed in Britain.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Who Put Bella in the Wych Elm?
shorts.covers: In 1943 four boys found a skeleton hidden inside a tree in Worcestershire, and soon messages began appearing on walls.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Lucky Luciano and the Commission
shorts.covers: A Sicilian-born gangster reorganised the American Mafia in the 1930s, and was later convicted on the evidence of the women who worked for him.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Aldrich Ames: The Spy Who Bought a Jaguar
shorts.covers: A CIA officer sold the names of America's agents in Moscow, and was caught partly because he was spending far more than he earned.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Sally Clark and the Misused Statistic
shorts.covers: In 1999 a solicitor was convicted of killing her two baby sons, on a statistic that was badly wrong, and was freed in 2003.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Tunnel Under the Brazilian Bank
shorts.covers: In 2005 a gang dug an eighty-metre tunnel from a fake gardening business into the Central Bank of Brazil in Fortaleza and took millions in cash.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Man Who Forged Vermeer
shorts.covers: Han van Meegeren sold fake Vermeer paintings to Nazi leader Hermann Goering, and after the war had to paint one in court to prove he was a forger, not a traitor.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Ladder That Solved the Lindbergh Case
shorts.covers: A wood scientist traced the home-made ladder used in the 1932 kidnapping of Charles Lindbergh's baby back to a timber yard and a floorboard.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Spy Who Escaped Wormwood Scrubs
shorts.covers: In 1966 the double agent George Blake climbed out of a London prison on a rope ladder of knitting needles and ended up in Moscow.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Patty Hearst: Victim or Robber?
shorts.covers: In 1974 a newspaper heiress was kidnapped by a radical group, and weeks later was filmed holding a rifle in a bank robbery.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Green River Killer
shorts.covers: For nearly twenty years a killer escaped police near Seattle, until in 2001 new DNA testing linked him to the crimes.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Hinterkaifeck Murders
shorts.covers: In 1922 a family on a remote Bavarian farm was killed, after days of footprints in the snow and strange noises in the attic.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Pablo Escobar's Last Rooftop
shorts.covers: The richest drug lord in history built an empire in Colombia, and was shot dead on a rooftop in Medellin in 1993.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Robert Hanssen: The Spy Inside the FBI
shorts.covers: For more than twenty years an FBI agent sold secrets to Moscow, leaving packages under a footbridge in a Virginia park.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Andrew Malkinson: Seventeen Years Wrongly Jailed
shorts.covers: In 2004 a man was convicted of a rape in Greater Manchester, and in 2023 DNA evidence finally cleared him.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Securitas Depot Robbery
shorts.covers: In 2006 a gang kidnapped a cash depot manager and his family in Kent, and walked away with more than fifty million pounds.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Bernie Madoff's Fifty-Billion-Dollar Lie
shorts.covers: For decades a respected Wall Street figure ran the largest investment fraud in history, until the 2008 crash made it impossible to hide.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Catching the Golden State Killer
shorts.covers: In 2018 investigators found a man who had committed crimes across California decades earlier, by matching DNA through a family history website.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: El Chapo's Tunnel
shorts.covers: In 2015 the drug lord Joaquin Guzman disappeared through a hole in his shower into a mile-long tunnel with a motorbike on rails.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Kidnapping of Freddy Heineken
shorts.covers: In 1983 the head of the Heineken beer company was kidnapped in Amsterdam and held in a hidden cell for three weeks.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: BTK and the Floppy Disk
shorts.covers: In 2005 a serial killer who had taunted police in Kansas for thirty years was caught by information hidden in a floppy disk he sent them.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Villisca Axe Murders
shorts.covers: In 1912 eight people were killed in a house in a small Iowa town, and no one was ever convicted.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Whitey Bulger: The Informant Who Ran Boston
shorts.covers: A Boston gangster spent years as an FBI informant while running his gang, then disappeared for sixteen years.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Mata Hari: Dancer, Spy or Scapegoat?
shorts.covers: In 1917 a famous dancer was shot by a French firing squad as a German spy, on evidence historians now question.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Lindy Chamberlain and the Dingo
shorts.covers: In 1980 a baby disappeared from a campsite near Uluru, and her mother was convicted of murder before a jacket found in the desert cleared her.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Walkie-Talkie Robbery
shorts.covers: In 1971 a radio enthusiast in London overheard robbers talking as they tunnelled into a Baker Street bank vault, and nobody believed him.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Theranos: The Blood Test That Did Not Work
shorts.covers: Elizabeth Holmes promised a machine that could run hundreds of tests from a drop of blood, and built a nine-billion-dollar company on it.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Brick Through the Windscreen
shorts.covers: In 2003 a brick thrown from a bridge killed a lorry driver in Surrey, and police found the thrower through a relative's DNA, the first conviction of its kind.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Great Libby Prison Escape
shorts.covers: In 1864 more than a hundred Union officers tunnelled out of a Confederate prison in Richmond, through a cellar full of rats.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Natascha Kampusch: Eight Years Hidden
shorts.covers: In 1998 a ten-year-old girl was taken on her way to school in Vienna, and in 2006 she ran from her captor's garden.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Son of Sam and the Parking Ticket
shorts.covers: In 1977 the gunman terrorising New York was traced through a parking ticket on his car near the scene of the last shooting.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Lord Lucan Vanishes
shorts.covers: In 1974 the family nanny was killed at a London house, and the aristocrat named by an inquest disappeared that night and was never seen again.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Gangster Brought Down by His Deputy
shorts.covers: John Gotti was called the Teflon Don because charges never stuck, until his own underboss testified against him in 1992.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Portland Spy Ring
shorts.covers: In 1961 police uncovered a Soviet spy ring working from a bungalow in a London suburb, with a radio hidden in the house.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Central Park Five
shorts.covers: In 1989 five teenagers were convicted of an attack in New York, and in 2002 the real attacker confessed and DNA confirmed it.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Knightsbridge Safe Deposit Robbery
shorts.covers: In 1987 a man rented a safe deposit box in London, then came back with friends, tied up the staff and emptied the vault.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Fake Heiress of New York
shorts.covers: Anna Sorokin posed as a rich German heiress called Anna Delvey and lived in luxury hotels on other people's money, until she was caught in 2017.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Flies That Found a Killer
shorts.covers: In thirteenth-century China, an investigator called Song Ci laid out the villagers' sickles in the sun, and the flies gathered on one.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Jack Sheppard: London's Escape Artist
shorts.covers: In the 1720s a young thief escaped from London's prisons four times, and thousands came to watch him hang.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Elizabeth Smart Comes Home
shorts.covers: In 2002 a fourteen-year-old was taken from her bedroom in Salt Lake City, and a TV appeal led to her rescue nine months later.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Unabomber's Brother
shorts.covers: In 1996 the man behind seventeen years of mail bombs was caught after his own brother recognised his writing in a newspaper.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Max Headroom Broadcast Hijack
shorts.covers: In 1987 someone in a mask broke into two Chicago television broadcasts, and the hijackers were never found.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Real Peaky Blinders
shorts.covers: Long before the television series, street gangs in Victorian Birmingham earned the name, and the truth is rougher than the drama.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Illegals: Spies Next Door
shorts.covers: In 2010 the FBI arrested ten Russian sleeper agents living ordinary lives in American suburbs, and swapped them in Vienna.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Sacco and Vanzetti
shorts.covers: In 1927 two Italian immigrants were executed in Massachusetts for a robbery and murder, after a trial that was criticised around the world.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Lufthansa Heist
shorts.covers: In 1978 robbers took millions in cash from a cargo building at New York's Kennedy Airport, and almost everyone involved was dead within months.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Bre-X: The Gold Mine Full of Nothing
shorts.covers: In the 1990s a Canadian company announced one of the biggest gold finds ever in Indonesia, and the samples turned out to have been salted with gold.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Two Men Called Will West
shorts.covers: In 1903 an American prison found two men with the same name and the same face, and it helped fingerprints replace body measurements.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Con Man Who Kept Escaping
shorts.covers: Steven Russell escaped from Texas prisons again and again by pretending to be a doctor, a judge and even a dying man.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Jaycee Dugard: Eighteen Years in a Backyard
shorts.covers: In 1991 an eleven-year-old was snatched from a street in California, and was found alive in 2009 because two police officers noticed something odd.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Lambeth Poisoner
shorts.covers: In 1892 a doctor poisoned women in south London, then wrote letters accusing others, and his own letters gave him away.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Black Dahlia
shorts.covers: In 1947 the body of a young woman was found in Los Angeles, and the case became one of the most famous unsolved murders in America.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Richardson Gang
shorts.covers: In 1960s south London a gang of brothers ran businesses and a reputation for brutal punishments, until a trial in 1967.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Gunpowder Plot
shorts.covers: In 1605 a group of conspirators hid barrels of gunpowder under the Houses of Parliament, and an anonymous letter gave them away.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Cardiff Three
shorts.covers: In 1990 three men were convicted of a Cardiff murder after a confession taken in hours of shouting, and later cleared.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: D.B. Cooper: The Hijacker Who Jumped
shorts.covers: In 1971 a man hijacked a plane over Washington state, took a ransom, and parachuted into the night. He was never identified.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Catch Me If You Can, Fact or Fiction?
shorts.covers: Frank Abagnale's story of posing as a pilot, doctor and lawyer became a Hollywood film, and researchers later found much of it was untrue.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Every Contact Leaves a Trace
shorts.covers: Edmond Locard set up one of the first crime laboratories in Lyon, and his simple idea that every contact leaves a trace still guides crime scenes.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Helicopter Escapes
shorts.covers: A French bank robber escaped from prison by helicopter, then used another helicopter to free his friends.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Wrong Woman: Muriel McKay
shorts.covers: In 1969 two brothers kidnapped a newspaper executive's wife in London by mistake, and became the first people in Britain convicted of murder without a body found.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Wallace Case
shorts.covers: In 1931 a Liverpool insurance agent went looking for an address that did not exist, and came home to find his wife murdered.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Princes in the Tower
shorts.covers: In 1483 two young princes disappeared inside the Tower of London, and the question of what happened to them has never been settled.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Great Brink's Robbery
shorts.covers: In 1950 eleven men robbed a Brink's depot in Boston of millions, and were caught days before the time limit for prosecution ran out.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: The Profumo Affair
shorts.covers: In 1963 a British government minister lied to Parliament about an affair, in a scandal tangled up with a Soviet naval attache.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case

shorts.title: Sam Hallam: Seven Years for Nothing
shorts.covers: In 2005 a teenager from east London was convicted of a murder on shaky identification evidence, and his conviction was quashed in 2012.
shorts.source: court records, contemporary newspaper reporting and published histories of the case
